# Lantern care

The lantern glazing collects a salt haze on every onshore wind, and the haze
is not visible from inside the lightroom at night. Clean the outer glazing
with fresh water and a chamois in daylight, before the haze can etch, and
never with the abrasive paste kept for the brass.

Measured over one winter: glazing washed weekly held its polish; glazing
washed monthly needed grinding twice. The weekly wash costs twenty minutes
and the grinding costs a fortnight, so the cheap habit is the expensive one
avoided.

The brass handrail and the pedestal collar are polished on a separate
schedule from the glazing, because the polish that suits brass will scratch
optical glass permanently. Keep the two cloths in different lockers. One
keeper who kept them in the same bag scratched a panel that then had to be
replaced.
